artifacts.summary: 13-phase plan for net-new git-push enforcement plus a single-use, HMAC-signed, target-bound consent grant minted only by a literal human prompt: grant library, /please mint hook, push guard + sanctioned wrapper, destructive-guard grant check, dual-template registration, five test suites, the /please command and rule narrowing, and the orchestrator relay leg.

user_decision.question: Consent-gated push: may a plain (non-force) push of the default branch be authorized by a /please grant, or should every push to the default branch stay categorically excluded as the research report recommended?
options: Admit plain non-force default-branch pushes under a valid grant; keep every force form on the default branch, bare --force anywhere, and all bulk/deletion refspecs categorically excluded (planner's recommendation - git-workflow.md's pre-existing Never Run is specifically force-to-master, and this repo's own working branch IS master, so a blanket exclusion would make the mechanism unusable here)
Exclude every push to the default branch from any grant, per the research report's stricter recommendation; a push from this repository would then always require a non-default branch
user_decision.recommended: Admit plain non-force default-branch pushes under a valid grant; keep every force form on the default branch, bare --force anywhere, and all bulk/deletion refspecs categorically excluded (planner's recommendation - git-workflow.md's pre-existing Never Run is specifically force-to-master, and this repo's own working branch IS master, so a blanket exclusion would make the mechanism unusable here)

memory_candidates.content: Install-once vs. merge-fragment settings registration is a live, recurring trap in this agent-system source store: agent-system/extensions/core/root-files/settings.json is INSTALL-ONCE (the root_files copier skips it whenever the target exists), so a hook registered only there can never reach an already-initialized consumer repo; merge-sources/settings-hooks.json is the add-only merge fragment that does reach existing repos. Any new PreToolUse/UserPromptSubmit hook must be registered in BOTH, each as its own dedicated single-command matcher object (object-level dedup keeps re-merges idempotent; appending into an existing shared '*' matcher's hooks array does not). guard-destructive-git.sh is itself a live instance of the gap - its Bash matcher exists only in root-files/settings.json. check-extension-docs.sh Rule P's check_settings_merge_source_coverage() detects this class but suppresses it (condition 3) whenever the hook is already live in the current repo's deployed tree, so the gap stays invisible in the repo that authored it.
